name: Higashi-Shinjuku
tagline: Shinjuku in 9 minutes and Shibuya in 10 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000.
summary: The station is in Shinjuku City, where Tokyo Metro and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 20 minutes to Otemachi, 9 minutes to Shinjuku, 10 minutes to Shibuya and 36 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. The station stands 30 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 10.0 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 30 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 22.2 m to 32.2 m, a difference of 10.0 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 2 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is less than 0.5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.

groceries.name: マルエツ 新宿六丁目店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 15 clinics and 20 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 都立大久保病院, about 10 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 広恵会春山外科病院, about 15 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line run through it. Toei Oedo Line also call here. The lines are split between operators (Tokyo Metro runs 1 line and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Toei Oedo Line runs at 147% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 中井→東中野, which this station is not on. Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line runs at 117%. Its busiest stretch is 要町→池袋, which this station is likewise not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥120,000 to ¥130,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥220,000 to ¥230,000 and 2LDK ¥310,000 to ¥320,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. What pushes the figure up: a small projected flood depth. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For how close the centre is, Shin-Okubo; for rail connections, Higashi-Shinjuku.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Higashi-Shinjuku. Shin-Okubo has only the JR Yamanote Line, so Higashi-Shinjuku is the better connected. To Shinjuku, for instance, Shin-Okubo is 6 minutes quicker. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥24,000 less at Shin-Okubo.

neighbours.lead: For the number of places to eat out, Seibu-Shinjuku; for rail connections, Higashi-Shinjuku.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Higashi-Shinjuku. Seibu-Shinjuku has only the Seibu Shinjuku Line, so Higashi-Shinjuku is the better connected. To Toranomon, for instance, Seibu-Shinjuku takes 15 minutes longer. A one-room flat also costs about ¥10,000 more at Seibu-Shinjuku. On the number of places to eat out, though, Seibu-Shinjuku comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: The data does not show a drawback particular to this station
noiseSources: 明治通り (2 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 12 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 4 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
